newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end brisk session mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end brisk session mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended a brisk volume day mixed, with June Standard and Poor's 500 futures slightly lower.

June reached a fresh record high early in the day at 849.50, spurred by buying from Wall Street firms on the open, but traders said interest quickly dried up. June cut gains soon after and trekked lower when Treasury bond futures sank on technical woes.
"Today was a pretty big move," one S&P 500 futures floor source said. "There was a lot of excitement this morning, but they were overbought and started drifting down with bonds."
June S&Ps fell as low as 836.50 on the afternoon decline, before recovering from the lows.
June S&Ps ended down 1.65 points at 842.90.
The floor source said strength in technology stocks lent support to S&Ps on the decline.

"We couldn't decide if we were going to remain firm with Nasdaq or follow the bonds," he said. "But I think we found a lot of support from the tech stocks," he said. June Nasdaq 100 index futures rallied sharply to a fresh record high, led by gains in Microsoft, Intel and Dell Computer Corp. June Nasdaq ended up 6.50 points at 952.75, in a 947.50 to 966.00 range.
Traders said the market was jittery after rallying on news Tuesday the U.S. Fed had left interest rates unchanged.
"A bunch of people got long on the outcome," another S&P 500 futures trader said. "I thought the move was overjustified and the market overbought," he said.
Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards showed estimated June S&P 500 futures volume at 86,000 contracts.
"We were really busy," one trading desk manager for a Japanese bank said.
Before S&Ps opened, the U.S. March trade gap was reported to have shrunk 19.3 percent to $8.51 billion.

At the close, NYSE Composites were down 1.35 at 437.80, KCBT Value Lines were up 1.15 at 741.95, Nikkeis were down 415 at 19,940, Midcap 400s were up 0.60 at 272.90, and Russell 2000s were up 0.80 at 372.30. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
